Section.Title: Runtime extensions
Section.Paragraph: Sia.Prelude extends the core ECS with maintained indexes, reactive lifecycles, cancellation, parallel jobs, snapshots, serialization, and actor-owned Worlds.

Section.Title: 1. Maintained indexes
Section.Paragraph: Reactors maintain derived indexes as the World changes. Hierarchy tracks parent-child relations, Aggregator groups entities, and Mapper resolves stable keys.
Destroying the root removes its descendants through the hierarchy reactor. The domain code stays small because the index owns the relationship.

Section.Title: 2. Reactive reconciliation
Section.Paragraph: A Reactive component describes the desired output. A flush preserves compatible entities, replaces changed data, and removes the output on unmount.
State may change several times before a flush. Reconciliation observes the final value and applies one consistent result.

Section.Title: 3. Higher-order events
Section.Paragraph: Higher-order events can cancel, pause, resume, or revert another event without coupling the sender to its handlers. This example intercepts termination for one entity.
Cancellation is scoped to one entity, one event type, and one dispatch. It does not replace the entity's normal lifecycle.

Section.Title: 4. Component event history
Section.Paragraph: EventSystemBase dispatches recorded event types. ComponentEventSystemBase also retains the value from before each component change.
Add, Set, and Remove form an ordered lifecycle. Every recorded event keeps its own previous value.

Section.Title: 5. Parallel processing
Section.Paragraph: Workers read the World in parallel and collect commands. The owning thread applies structural changes after all jobs complete.
The result is deterministic even when discovery order is not. No entity is destroyed until the parallel phase has ended.

Section.Title: 6. Live views and snapshots
Section.Paragraph: A SubWorld exposes a live, read-only query. A snapshot copies selected data so another thread can read it without touching the source World.
The live view follows each update. The snapshot changes only when extracted, so it may be older but remains internally consistent.

Section.Title: 7. Thread-local context
Section.Paragraph: Context<T> provides one thread-local resource to each worker. Jobs reuse the resource owned by the thread that executes them.
Scheduling may change execution order, but each job still receives the context associated with its worker thread.

Section.Title: 8. Serialization
Section.Paragraph: BinaryWorldSerializer writes host metadata and MemoryPack component data. GZip compresses the stream; the deserializer reconstructs the World.
Unmanaged components serialize directly. Components with references need an explicit formatter and a stable schema.

Section.Title: 9. World actor
Section.Paragraph: WorldActor assigns one thread to a World. Other threads post work to its mailbox, and shutdown drains pending work before disposal.
Posting does not make arbitrary mutation thread-safe. It routes mutations through the thread that owns the World.

Section.Title: A clear ownership model
Section.Paragraph: Components remain the source of truth. Indexes derive state, Reactive reconciles lifecycles, snapshots cross thread boundaries, and one owner applies structural changes.
